name: Dick Stevenson Redidence

nadir.desc: The property consists of a large primary residence with a gray shingle roof and multiple roof planes|A curved paved driveway leads from the street to a large paved courtyard and garage|A water feature and landscaped garden sit at the rear of the house|A small detached structure stands in the side yard|Open lawn and scattered trees surround the building|The North Umpqua River is adjacent to the neighborhood.

alpha.desc: The front of the residence faces Hidden Valley Lane with a curved paved driveway leading to a courtyard and garage doors|The house has a gray shingle roof and a covered entry|Trees stand in a landscaped island in the driveway|Open lawn and additional trees line the side of the lot.

bravo.desc: The left side of the residence shows the long garage wing, the paved courtyard, and the rear water feature|A small detached structure sits in the side yard with a walkway from the house|Open lawn and trees run along this side|The driveway curves from the street to the courtyard.

charlie.desc: The rear of the residence shows the water feature, landscaped garden, and rear elevation of the house|Dense trees line the rear property edge toward the river|Open ground is present beyond the garden|The paved courtyard and driveway remain visible at the front.

delta.desc: The right side of the residence shows the garage doors, courtyard, and side elevation of the house|Trees stand along the driveway and street|The rear water feature is visible at the far end|Open lawn surrounds the side of the structure.

considerations: neighboring homes, open lawn, and the North Umpqua River along one edge of the area. The rear garden and water feature occupy space behind the house. Trees screen portions of the street approach and the rear edge. A small detached structure sits in the side yard. Movement around the house is generally open except at the landscaped rear.
clarifications: Does the driveway terminate at the courtyard, or is there vehicle access around the house? Are there any gates at the street entrance?
